title: 10 Tips for Riding your Motorcycle Safely this Summer
metaDescription: motorcycle insurance
excerpt: Although riding a motorcycle might be exciting, safety should always come first. At Tennessee Auto Insurance Agency, our client's safety is in our best interests. So, we have compiled a list of tips to help you ride your motorcycle safely this summer. 1. Keep hydrated
html:
Although riding a motorcycle might be exciting, safety should always come first. At Tennessee Auto Insurance Agency, our client's safety is in our best interests. So, we have compiled a list of tips to help you ride your motorcycle safely this summer.


1. Keep hydrated


The most significant fluid in the human body is water. When exposed to heat from the outside, the body begins to sweat. The upshot of this is that the body becomes dehydrated. Dehydration can result in fatigue, headaches, irritability, and poor focus. By making frequent stops to drink water, you can prevent this from becoming fatal in severe situations. The journey will be safer since a hydrated body will produce a focused mind. Dehydration is still a problem, even if you drink water simultaneously. You should consume water regularly.


In this circumstance, you can use a hydration pack. A hydration pack is a hydration device with a bladder where water can be stored that is designed as a waist pack or backpack. With these hydration packs, you always have access to water to keep hydrated. To be clear, we advise only drinking water and ORS or electrolytes. Do not drink tea, coffee, soft drinks, or energy drinks because they further dehydrate the body.


Furthermore, avoid cycling, if possible, during the hottest hours of the day because high heat can cause exhaustion and other health problems. If you must ride in the heat, wear proper clothing and pause frequently.


2. Dress in ventilated clothing


In terms of summer clothes, ventilation is crucial. When it comes to comfort, the base layer is vital. This layer needs to be moisture-wicking to vaporize sweat and absorb it, keeping the body dry and cool. Even though cotton is a lightweight fiber that absorbs moisture but does not expel it, wearing it can make you feel damp. Nylon and polyester materials, on the other hand, are excellent at absorbing and releasing moisture, making them your go-to base layer option in the summer.


Summertime does not automatically mean that you may ignore safety. Wearing your helmet, riding jacket, riding pants, gloves, and boots is always required. But the material you choose should encourage airflow and keep you feeling fabulous. All sweat evaporates when wearing riding jackets, pants, and perforated gloves made of ventilated textiles with mesh inserts. This keeps the body moisturized and cool while assisting in stabilizing body temperature. You can use a cooling vest over time. These vests cool both the surface and the interior of the body. Damp neck tubes will also keep you cool and cozy.


You might have a tinted visor on your helmet to protect your eyes from the sun. These visors will shield you from the sun's glare and dangerous UV rays. Using such visors, you might ride for extended periods and experience less eye fatigue.


Always protect your head and eyes by donning a DOT-approved helmet, eye shields, a rugged jacket, gloves, long pants, and over-the-ankle boots. The severity of injuries in an accident can be considerably decreased with the proper riding equipment.


Additionally, utilize your motorcycle's headlights at all times, including during the day, and wear bright or reflective clothes. It is easier for other drivers to see you on the road when you are more visible.


3. Inspect the tires for damage


The only point of contact between a car and the road is its tires. It is essential to take precautions to prevent the motorcycle from skidding and the road's tremendous heat from blowing out the tires. The tire pressure rises by 1.4 PSI for every 10% change in temperature. This might not seem a big concern, but it might make the difference between correctly inflated and overinflated tires. You should not disregard that a tire's sidewalls and tread harden more than usual when it is overinflated and loses contact with the road. This change in footprint may result in traction and performance loss, roughing the ride and impairing the motorcycle's handling and braking capabilities.


You should maintain proper tire pressure, repair worn-out tires, and take appropriate breaks to allow the tires to cool down in case they become overheated to prevent the tires from bursting due to heat. Additionally, you should follow the tires' speed rating and load capacity.


Conduct a complete pre-ride examination before each ride. Ensure all lights and signals are operational, check the brakes, oil, and fluid levels, and inspect the tires for proper pressure and condition.


4. Watch out for asphalt melting on tarmac roads


When subjected to constant, intense heat, the asphalt coating on roadways tends to soften. Asphalt softening can result in uneven and slick roads, making them hazardous. The weight of the traffic-moving vehicles may also impact this softening. When you drive over a section like this, the ripple effects of the motion of these large trucks on the road may cause your bike to become unsteady. Be cautious and keep an eye out for the strength of the road.


5. Taking necessary rests at regular times


You will benefit from careful planning for the ride in the summer. Starting early is always advised when the temperature is still reasonably low. Your primary priorities should be finding some cover and unwinding while the sun is straight overhead. Riding in extreme heat should be avoided because it can constantly wear you out to fight the summer heat. You must stop frequently to re-hydrate and give the motorcycle time to cool down.

Regular breaks also guarantee that you maintain focus and finish the route without incident.


6. Keep Your Focus and Alertness


Keep a vigilant eye on the road and the area around you. Be extra cautious at crossroads and when changing lanes, and avoid distractions like using a phone while riding. Additionally, follow all traffic regulations and posted speed restrictions. Following traffic laws might help keep you safe because speeding contributes to motorcycle accidents.


  • Keep an eye out for road hazards, including gravel, potholes, oil spills, and debris. These dangers can be more common in the summer.
  • Avoid Driving Under the Influence. Do not drive under the influence of drugs, alcohol, or any other substance that slows your reaction time or compromises your judgment.
  • Turn signals are a straightforward way to express your intentions to other drivers.
  • Always bike conservatively to anticipate and avoid potential hazards, assuming other drivers will not see you.

7. Pay attention to wildlife


Wildlife may be more active in warmer months, particularly at dawn and dusk. In rural locations, use caution and be ready to respond if an animal enters your path.


8. Attend a Refresher Course


Consider enrolling in a motorcycle safety course or refresher training to improve your riding abilities and enforce safe practices.


9. Keep up with local weather updates


Before starting a ride, check the weather forecast and be ready for rapid changes in the weather.


10. Purchase motorcycle insurance


Motorcycle insurance should be something you think about if you buy a motorcycle. Thinking about the risks before riding your bike on the road is essential. Accidents can happen at any time and are expensive to repair. Having motorcycle insurance can save you from paying significant out-of-pocket costs after an accident. To learn more, click here.


You may have a safer and more pleasurable summer of motorcycle riding by heeding their advice and putting safety first. To receive a quote for your motorcycle insurance, click here.

title: 14 Safety Tips for Nighttime Driving
metaDescription: Driving at night is substantially riskier than during the day, so it's not just paranoia.
excerpt: Driving at night is substantially riskier than during the day, so it's not just paranoia. A fatal accident is three times more likely to occur at night than during the day. html:
Driving at night is substantially riskier than during the day, so it's not just paranoia. A fatal accident is three times more likely to occur at night than during the day. We cannot see as well in the dark, which is the leading cause.


You have less time and room to stop since you can see less of the road before you. Ironically, some types of light, such as the glare from too bright lights, might exacerbate the issue. But additional elements make nighttime driving more difficult.


This post will go over some suggestions for increasing your nighttime driving safety.


1. Drive in Defense Mode


After nightfall, drinking and driving are riskier. Nearly four times more fatal crashes involving alcohol-impaired driving occur at night than during the day. Of course, you should never drive after drinking, regardless of the time of day, and the same goes for distracted driving. However, you need to be extra vigilant regarding defensive driving at night.


2. Combat Exhaustion


Most crashes involving sleepy drivers occur between midnight and six in the morning. Therefore, stay vigilant during these times and be aware that there may be tired drivers on the road. Obtain some caffeine, halt for the night, or relax in a secure location. Other activities that some drivers claim to be beneficial include singing or talking to themselves while driving, turning on the radio (but not too loudly), and occasionally rolling down the windows for fresh air.


3. Steer Clear of two-lane roads


Due to the headlights of oncoming vehicles, the lower total illumination, and the fact that these routes frequently have more abrupt curves and hills than a freeway, two-lane highways may be the "worst-case scenario" for nighttime glare. Take a safer path at night if you can.


4. Clean Your View


Windshields that are dirty or broken may scatter light and amplify glare's effects. Additionally, the group notes that having dusty or broken headlights might reduce visibility and glare at approaching vehicles. As a result, routinely clean your windshield and headlights. You can use a headlight cleaning kit.


5. Be Patient


Due to reduced visibility and slower reaction times, speeding-related crashes cause 37% more fatalities when driving at night than during the day. For instance, even at 40 mph, you need 190 feet to stop when your headlight generally illuminates 160 feet in front of you. Consider conditions like visibility when adjusting your speed.


6. Correctly Angle Your Headlights


If the beams slant down too far, you will lose some required illumination while driving. However, if they tilt too far, they risk blinding approaching drivers. You should take the initiative to ensure that your headlights are oriented appropriately, even if your state's annual inspection tests don't include a headlight angle check. "Normally, this is not a DIY project. We suggest you seek assistance from your car dealer or a repair shop.


7. Modify the Interior Lighting


Glancing from the dashboard to the dark road in front of you can be confusing if your dashboard lights are too bright. Use your visors at night to protect you from glare and street lighting, and dim the interior lights so that essential controls are visible but not distracting. Many modern vehicles include mirrors that automatically reduce the brightness of bright light reflections.


8. Utilize High Beams When Necessary


Although rarely used, high beams are beneficial on open roads, especially in rural areas. Just remember to turn them off if you're following another car and to dim them when you're 500 feet or less from an approaching vehicle (so you don't momentarily blind the other driver). When shopping for a new car, we advise you to seek adaptive lighting systems, which automatically change your highlights in response to the presence of other vehicles.


9. Face the Correct Direction


While you should constantly keep your eyes on the road, try not to stare at approaching headlights or maintain a fixed glance. The right edge of the road or lane markers can serve as guidance to help you keep on course when coming from an approaching vehicle to prevent being blinded by its headlights. Once you have passed the approaching car, raise your gaze back up.


10. Be Aware Of Wildlife


Animal collisions frequently occur at dusk or night and are more frequent during the winter. You may see an animal's sparkling eyes with the aid of your powerful lasers. The safest approach to preventing a collision when you see one is to slow down and stop, not to swerve.


Nighttime is when animals are more active, especially in rural regions. If you notice any animals or luminous eyes reflecting in your headlights, pay attention to the sides of the road and proceed cautiously.


11. Test and use your lights


Regularly test your lights, including the high beams, daytime running lights, turn signals, and brake lights. And remember to utilize your headlights to keep visible; you should do so not only when it's dark out but also in inclement weather like rain, snow, and hail.


12. Protect your eyes


Get a yearly eye exam; as people age, glare threatens their eyesight more. At night, you could also require a different prescription.


13. Extend your following distance


Unlike what you would do during the day, allow a wider following distance. As a result, you have more time to respond to unexpected halts or impediments. Some motorists can be tired or struggle with nighttime vision. Keep an eye out for unpredictable driving patterns and give them more room.


14. Take breaks

Take frequent pauses if you're traveling late at night to prevent weariness. Stretch your legs and stop at well-lit rest stops to allow yourself to relax.


In conclusion


Due to diminished vision, driving at night might create particular difficulties. We've talked about precautions to take when driving at night. Among them is ensuring your headlights are functionally sound: ensuring that they are clear, positioned correctly, and emitting enough light.


Any dim or broken bulbs should be replaced. Remember that it's preferable to find a safe spot to pull over and relax than to continue driving if you feel overly weary or find it difficult to concentrate.

excerpt: What suggestions do we have for new and student drivers? Everyone can recall the hype of becoming a new driver and entering the road for the first time. Nothing compares to the sense of liberation or adventure that lies ahead.
html:
What suggestions do we have for new and student drivers?


Everyone can recall the hype of becoming a new driver and entering the road for the first time. Nothing compares to the sense of liberation or adventure that lies ahead. Buying a new car, however, can be a little more complicated; so much information is available that it is normal to feel confused or overloaded.


We have all been there, so we came up with five essential questions to help you decide and ensure you have the best possible start to your driving career.


There are several things to consider when choosing a car for a rookie or inexperienced driver. These include safety features, handling simplicity, dependability, and price.


In this article, we will discuss a few things to keep in mind when getting your vehicle and give examples on some commonly purchased cars for inexperienced and beginner drivers


Automatic or manual?


Previously, most automobiles had manual transmissions, meaning you had to operate the gear shift to move the car manually. The popularity of automatic transmissions, in which the vehicle changes gears independently, has dramatically increased in recent years. This is due to several factors, including the fact that automatic automobiles are more pleasant to drive in traffic and that many people believe they are more straightforward for new drivers to use because they do not present the usual difficulties of starting on a slope or cutting off at traffic signals.


It is crucial to remember that automatic vehicles are typically more expensive to buy and that driving efficiency may suffer with older models. Significantly, for new drivers, passing a driving test in an automatic car limits your ability to drive to those with automatic transmissions, whereas passing a test in a manual vehicle allows you to drive both types of cars. Ask your driving instructor for more information about both choices.


Electric, hybrid, diesel, or gas?


People talk a lot about how we fuel our cars for economic and environmental reasons. Your tastes, annual miles, and spending plan for purchases and fuel can all have an impact. While the USA has made great strides in terms of charging stations, where you live may also have an impact on your decisions.


Recent years have seen new electric car registrations, which suggests that over the following few years, the used car market should see an increase in the number of electric vehicles. In the interim, statistical data can assist you in reducing your options and determining which is the best choice for you.


Minivan or Mini?


You must take your time to select the ideal car size for you. Many newly licensed or learning drivers start modestly, so they feel confident when negotiating tight turns or fitting into confined parking spaces.


However, you might decide to move up through the models based on your commute, your family's size, or your personal preferences; speaking to a salesperson in a car dealership will help you determine the ideal vehicle for you. It might be a good idea to bring your wheelchair, stroller, bicycle, or set of golf clubs to the car showroom to see if they will fit in the trunk. If it does not, you will realize that this is not the car for you.


Is it brand new or used?


The first car most individuals purchase is typically used. Because new cars lose more value over their first few years on the road, used vehicles are typically more economical. With a used automobile, you won't have to worry as much about the occasional ding on the paint job; most vehicles will accumulate bumps and bruises over time.


If you have a larger budget, there are advantages to purchasing a new automobile, like a warranty, a service package, and cheap interest rates on loans. To ensure you get the ideal vehicle for you and your situation, visit your neighborhood dealership and use national consumer guidance resources.


Third Party, Fire and Theft, Third Party Only, or Fully Comprehensive?


All drivers, whether novices, recently licensed drivers, or professionals, must have car insurance. The most common insurance options are comprehensive, third-party, fire and theft, and third-party only, but it's not always obvious which is best for you. These insurances provide security and peace of mind, but depending on your situation, financial situation, and vehicle, one may be more suitable for you than the other. Check out our insurance page for a breakdown of the differences between these policies.


Getting reliable car insurance is the most crucial step. Anyone can have an accident; if something goes wrong, you will want someone on your side. Policy holders at Tennessee Auto Insurance receive specialized claims. This means that you deal with just one person from the minute something goes wrong until we fix it. Additionally, most claims are resolved amicably, giving you the peace of mind you need.


Now let us discuss some of the frequently purchased cars by new drivers and why people go for them.


Honda Civic: The Honda Civic is renowned for its dependability, efficiency in terms of fuel use, and safety features. It has a pleasant interior, easy handling, and superb visibility.


Toyota Corolla: Thanks to its reputation for dependability, affordability, and safety, the Toyota Corolla is a well-liked option among novice drivers. It offers simple controls and a comfortable ride.


Ford Focus: The small Ford Focus compromises affordability and handling. It boasts excellent safety ratings and has cutting-edge safety features, including lane-keeping assistance and blind-spot monitoring.


Hyundai Elantra: Popular for its affordability, fuel efficiency, and safety features, the Hyundai Elantra is a popular car. It rides smoothly, features easy-to-use technologies, and has a cozy cabin.


Mazda3: The Mazda3 has received plaudits for its striking appearance, sporty handling, and safety features. It provides a nice balance of power and fuel economy.


VolkswagenGolf: The Volkswagen Golf is a practical hatchback with a good track record for handling and safety. It provides many available safety features, comfort, and adequate interior space.


In conclusion


Remember that new and inexperienced drivers should prioritize safety and select vehicles that fit their demands and budget. As these features can improve road safety, it is also advised to consider cars with advanced driver-assistance systems such as automated emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, and blind-spot monitoring.

html:
What Is Renters Insurance?


Renters insurance helps protect tenants from unexpected occurrences. Instances like theft, break-in, or a visitor's accident are not preventable, so you need renters insurance. This article will discuss three coverages in a renters insurance policy: personal belongings, liabilities, and additional living costs.


Personal property coverage


Personal property coverage can assist in defraying the expense of replacing your belongings in the event of an unexpected loss or destruction. According to the Insurance Information Institute, this protection typically relates to hazards such as fire. For instance, this coverage can assist you in covering the expense of replacing your clothing and furniture if they are destroyed in a fire. However, keep in mind that coverage limits—the highest amount your policy can reimburse you for losses of personal property — will remain in effect.


If your renter's insurance policy includes personal property coverage, it can assist in covering the cost of replacing your lost goods. Items taken during a break-in at your rental property or even items taken from outside your rental are usually covered by this policy. For instance, your renters insurance personal property coverage could assist in covering the cost of replacing any lost or stolen personal goods, such as a gaming system, from your vehicle.


Keep in mind that a deductible typically applies to personal property coverage. This means that before your insurer will contribute to the loss, you must pay a specific sum to repair or replace the protected item.


Properly study your insurance coverage to determine what might or might not be covered. Also, consider all you possess. The value of your possessions can build up quickly. How much would it cost to replace them if they were damaged or lost?


When obtaining a renters insurance policy, you may have a few options when choosing personal property coverage. Here are some things to remember:


You should choose coverage thresholds that are suitable for your circumstances. For example, inventorying the items you keep in your apartment or house will help you determine the worth of your possessions and the appropriate level of personal property coverage.


You might also need to choose the type of personal property insurance to buy. For example, items are typically covered up to their current market value (after depreciation) under an actual cash value insurance policy. However, after a covered loss, a policy offering replacement cost coverage could assist you in paying to replace your belongings at current retail prices.


Things not covered under the personal property coverage


A typical renters insurance policy offers limited protection for particular possessions, such as jewelry or a coin collection. To help protect your valuables, you can supplement your policy with additional coverage known as scheduled personal property coverage. Consult our local insurance agent to assess whether this coverage suits your needs.

Liability protection


Another type of protection that is frequently included in a renters insurance policy is liability coverage. If you are held legally accountable for someone else's injuries or property damage, this coverage may prevent you from paying some expenses out of pocket.


Liability insurance may assist in covering the costs if, for instance, your child accidentally throws a ball through a neighbor's window, your dog scratches your neighbor's fence, or you are held responsible for a visitor's medical bills after they slip and fall in your rented house or apartment.


The amount your insurance policy pays out following an insured loss is subject to limits, much like other coverages. Make sure your policy meets your needs by reading it to understand how much range it offers. If you determine that you might benefit from additional coverage, your insurance agent can assist you in adjusting the limits.


Additional living costs


When you rent a house or an apartment, you usually have a place to live until the end of your contract. But what if, for example, a fire damages your rented house and makes a living there impossible? Renters insurance could be helpful in this situation.


Extra living expenses are typically covered by renters insurance. After a covered loss, this coverage aids in covering any additional expenses you may incur due to being unable to live in the rental property. Examples of covered costs include hotel charges or extra meal expenses over regular pay. Check your policy to see how much additional living expenses coverage you have in place and review the risks that your policy might cover.



How to submit a claim for renters insurance


Here are some suggestions to remember if you need to submit a claim for renters insurance. However, remember that the procedure for filing your claims may change depending on the degree of damage.


-Report the claim to your insurance company as soon as you can.

-Prevent more harm to your possessions.

-Discuss any potential urgent repairs with your agent.

-Your agent will inquire about the damage and respond to any questions you might have about the procedure.

-Talk with your agent about the coverage and restrictions of your policy to see which ones apply to your circumstances.

-Before repairs are started, list damaged things in writing and take pictures or videos.


You may have to pay a deductible before renters insurance begins to cover a covered loss. Your deductible level is frequently correlated with the premium you pay to maintain your insurance coverage. Generally speaking, the higher your deductible for each covered loss, the lower your premium. Your coverage will specify your deductible and premium, which may be changed to fit your needs and budget. Click here to get a quote.


Although renters insurance can assist in protecting you and your possessions, you should be aware that it frequently does not cover the actual residence you are living in. While you, the renter, are often responsible for protecting the items you keep inside, landlord insurance is designed to assist in securing the owner's home. Like other insurance policies, landlord insurance may provide the policyholder with liability protection but usually does not cover tenants.

title: Never Leave These Things In Your Car
metaDescription: Never leave these things in your car:   We tend to forget some things in the car or think keeping them will be a good idea.

html:
Never leave these things in your car:


We tend to forget some things in the car or think keeping them will be a good idea. This article has compiled a list of things to never keep in the car, from food to documents to pets. We will discuss it all.


A significant reason you can't keep some of these items in the car is that temperatures can rapidly change in the vehicle. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration claims that in just 10 minutes, the temperature inside your automobile can rise by as much as 20 degrees. According to the American Veterinary Medical Association, on a day with a temperature of 95 degrees, it can reach a whopping 140 degrees after an hour. Naturally, that can harm kids and animals, but it can also cause issues with everything from food to combustible objects.


A friend left a bottle of unopened wine in her car overnight. When she came to her car in the morning, she saw that the wine bottle had broken and had wine all over her back seat. The wine stained her heart; she could never get it out. You can imagine how an innocent wine stain would decrease the value of her car if she decided to sell. Also, she spent a lot of money trying to get the stain out and missed out on a bottle of wine. Extreme temperatures have the potential to damage a variety of objects when left in the heat or cold, in addition to popping corks.


1. Food and Drinks


Like cork-sealed wine bottles, soda cans can cause issues in hot or cold cars. Furthermore, candy bars and ice cream chocolates can quickly melt in the heat and stain your vehicle.


According to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), bacteria that cause illnesses can grow in your food if you leave it in extreme heat, like in your car. So limit the time your groceries stay in the car to an hour.


Also, leaving food and beverages in your car might attract pests like ants or rodents that can harm your car's interior or pose a health risk.


2. Sunscreen


Packing a tube of sunscreen is usually a good idea, but be cautious about leaving the bottle in your car since the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) notes that exposing sunscreen to high temperatures can reduce its shelf life.


Furthermore, if the heat blows the cap open, your protective SPFs may lose effectiveness and become a huge, stinky mess.


3. Aerosols like hairspray or deodorant


A recommended storage temperature is listed on cans of hairspray, deodorant, spray paint, and similar items. Pressurized cans are susceptible; if exposed to temperatures outside that range, the contents may expand, and the can may shatter or explode. If the can explodes, it can damage something in your car.


4. Lighters


Although lighters are small, they have a powerful punch when heated. When exposed to intense heat, the combustible fuel inside these tiny plastic tubes might expand and break through the lighter's shell, posing a fire risk.


It's debatable if the heat in the car will lead to combustion, but why take a chance? Generally speaking, we advise you not to keep flammable liquids in your vehicle, especially in the summer.


5. Plastic bottles


A viral video from Idaho Power showed that a transparent water bottle inside the car amplified the sun's rays, which began burning the car seat.


Additionally, plastic bottles often contain bisphenol A (BPA), a potentially hazardous substance. BPA is safe, according to the FDA, at the present levels of exposure in food. However, you do not want to risk adding more of this chemical to your beverage because studies have shown that higher temperatures cause a greater release of BPA from plastics.


6. Electronics


Why leave your smartphone in a hot car when you would never consider leaving home without it? Numerous phone manufacturers provide recommended temperature ranges and advise against taking your device in your vehicle, where it may malfunction or begin to sustain damage.


Also, you might need your phone for something urgent. So never leave your phone in the car. Unfortunately, your phone and other devices can also attract thieves to enter your vehicle and steal your devices and your car.


Never leave anything of value in your car, including jewelry, gadgets, cash, and credit cards. This is because if you leave these things out in the open, robbers can come looking for them and break into your automobile.


7. Batteries


Battery manufacturers advise avoiding storing their products in hot environments because doing so might cause leakage or breakage in addition to capacity loss. The CDC section that regulates toxic substances states that battery acid is hazardous when inhaled and highly corrosive, which can be bad news for your health and the interior of your automobile. The best action is to keep acidic objects away from the console and inside your car.


8. Children and Pets


Do not leave your children or pets in the car. The heat might hurt them. Severe heat can cause heat stroke or hypothermia in pets and kids, and even if you leave the AC on, leaving children and pets unattended in your car is always a bad idea.


Leaving kids or pets alone in a car can also be against the law and lead to criminal penalties.


9. Important documents


Never leave your driver's license, passport, social security card, or vehicle registration in your vehicle. These records might be used fraudulently or for identity theft.


10. Medications


Medications should never be left in a car, particularly in hot or cold weather, as these conditions might reduce their effectiveness or cause them to degrade. Some medicines might also appeal to thieves.


In conclusion


Several things can hurt you if you leave them in the car, so it is best not to leave them in the car in the first place. For example, they can affect you health-wise, decrease the value of your vehicle, or cause us to lose your car and other valuables. Therefore, we recommend you empty the trash every time you leave the vehicle and ensure you do not keep these things in your car again.

At Tennessee Auto Insurance Agency, we think you must understand your car insurance to make confident decisions. Asking the right questions is always an excellent place to start because it ensures you get the necessary coverage.


Car insurance can seem confusing. So, understanding how it operates is crucial. Therefore, we have compiled a list of questions you may ask while speaking with your auto insurance provider.


1. Am I eligible for any auto discounts?


You can reduce your auto insurance cost by utilizing some providers' auto discounts.

Typical reductions include:


  • Multi-Car Discount

  • Combined Discount (bundle more than one product like auto and home or renters)

  • Discount for payments deducted from your bank account or paid in installments

  • Discount for receiving your bill by email (paperless bill)

  • Online insurance purchases

  • Military Discount

  • Student Discount

  • Safe driving


You may ask your insurance provider to evaluate your policy to ensure you receive all the discounts you qualify for.


2. What does my current auto insurance policy not cover?


Check your policy's details with your auto insurance provider. Finally, based on your needs, consider what you want to add. These extra coverages are not included in typical auto insurance policies.


Gap Coverage: This insurance will pay the balance due on your loan or lease if your car is totaled or stolen. That is if your vehicle's worth is less than the amount still owed.


24-Hour Roadside Help: Enjoy peace of mind knowing help is only a phone call away. The 24-hour roadside assistance can assist if your car breaks down, locks you out of your vehicle, or if you need a jump start or a tow.


Rental Car Reimbursement: This assists in covering the cost of a rental automobile while your car is getting fixed after an accident.


3. Do I have enough insurance? What coverages does my insurance include?


Ask these questions to find out the level of your automobile insurance.


  • What is my state-mandated minimum for auto insurance?

  • Is the expense of having comprehensive and collision coverage worth the cash value of my car?

  • Will the state-mandated minimum insurance cover all of my assets if I am at fault for an accident? -Remember that the liability coverage you receive should be sufficient to cover your assets.

  • Would my health insurance cover my medical costs if I have an accident? -If not, you might want to increase to some insurance policies, such as Personal Injury Protection (PIP) and medical payments coverage (MedPay). No matter who was at fault, these can assist in covering your medical costs following a vehicle accident. If an uninsured driver strikes you, the uninsured motorist coverage may also cover your medical bills.


4. What are my deductible costs?


If you have collision and comprehensive coverage and suffer a covered loss, you are responsible for paying your deductible. Having this cash set aside will enable you to pay for it in an emergency.


Please be aware that while raising your deductible may result in cheaper insurance costs, decreasing it may result in higher prices. So be sure to consider your alternatives and choose the solution that best suits you.


5. Am I protected if the car accident is my fault?


You may be held financially liable for an auto accident that you caused in which one or more people suffered significant injuries. This also includes covering their medical and auto repair expenses. The good news is that liability coverage can assist in defraying these expenses.


Note that bare minimum liability limits may not be sufficient in severe accidents. You might have to come up with extra cash if an accident loss exceeds your limits.


6. When will my insurance renew?


You need to know the date of your insurance renewal because:


  • It helps you know when your bills are due.

  • The best time to determine whether to keep your coverage or acquire estimates from other carriers is before the renewal.

  • You can purchase a new one before your current insurance expires.

  • It is an excellent time to discuss your policy's coverage with your agent, confirm any discounts, and make any necessary changes.


7. Should I get a telematics device?


Telematics equipment monitors your car's speed, mileage, total driving time, braking, acceleration, and other factors. These gadgets can be an app on your phone or a plug-in device for your car.


These gadgets can help safe drivers since they can get discounts for safe driving. These tools can also assist drivers in becoming more conscious of their driving and making positive changes.


8. Does my insurance cover me if my car is stolen?


Your insurance should assist in paying for the costs associated with your stolen vehicle if you have comprehensive coverage.


Comprehensive can help in two different ways:


  • Car was not found: Comprehensive can cover the cost of the stolen car's market value.

  • Car found: The vehicle's repairs will be partly assisted by Comprehensive.


Remember that you will be responsible for the comprehensive deductible from your coverage in both situations.


9. Will my insurance company cover the cost of a new car if my car is totaled?


You have coverage for a covered loss if you have comprehensive and collision insurance. A car is generally regarded as totaled if:


  • There is no way to fix it to make driving safe again.

  • The cost of the repairs exceeded the value of the vehicle.


Please be aware that the value of your car is determined using its pre-accident value minus your deductible. Therefore, comprehensive and collision insurance will only cover up to this sum.


At Tennessee Auto Insurance Agency, we provide insurance to aid you if your new car is totaled.

See how much you can save on auto insurance by purchasing what you need. Then, you can get a quote in less than 10 minutes. Click here to get a quote.


In conclusion


Ask your auto insurance provider the following questions:

  • Am I eligible for any auto discounts?

  • What does my current auto insurance policy not cover?

  • Do I have enough insurance? What coverages does my insurance include?

  • What are my deductible costs?

  • Am I protected if the car accident is my fault?

  • When will my insurance renew?

  • Should I get a telematics device?

  • Does my insurance cover me if my car is stolen?

  • Will my insurance company cover the cost of a new car if my car is totaled?


Asking these questions will enable you to make decisions with confidence.

title: Actions To Take In The Event Of A Car Accident

Actions to take in the event of a car accident


You might wish to take some actions after an automobile accident to ensure your safety, comply with the la
excerpt: Actions to take in the event of a car accident You might wish to take some actions after an automobile accident to ensure your safety, comply with the law, and begin the insurance claim procedure. Feeling anxious after an accident is normal, but taking these precautions can reduce anxiety.
html:
Actions to take in the event of a car accident


You might wish to take some actions after an automobile accident to ensure your safety, comply with the law, and begin the insurance claim procedure.


Feeling anxious after an accident is normal, but taking these precautions can reduce anxiety. You can then focus on preparing your vehicle's smooth and speedy repair with your insurance provider.


This article will discuss the most important things to do if you are involved in a car accident.



1. Verify the health and safety of your passengers


If you are not too hurt to move, see if the other people in your car need help. Then, call the emergency services or request that a bystander do so if anyone is hurt. You can also go to the sidewalk or the side of the road if you can.


Pull your vehicle to the side of the road if you can drive because leaving it in the middle of the road is dangerous. Alternatively, leave it alone and find protection for yourself.


2. Keep your cool


Breathe in first, then out. Take a minute to evaluate the situation. It is crucial to remain calm if you feel hurt or in danger. You can handle things better if you are relaxed and composed.


3. Call the police


It is important to notify the police immediately, even in a minor accident with no injuries. In addition, call 911 because you need to submit official police reports to file an auto insurance claim.


You must give the police the following information:


  • Your full name and contact details

  • Insurance company name and policy number

  • License plate number and driver's license

  • Model, kind, and color of the car

  • Place of the accident


Furthermore, you must remain on the scene because it is illegal to leave an accident scene before the police arrive.


Get the police officer's name and badge number when they arrive. Then, ask the on-duty policeman where you may get a copy of the accident report.


4. Record the scene


Capture pictures of the harmed vehicles, the damaged property, the people involved, the license plates, and the location markers. The photos will help you remember the incident when filing your insurance claim.


Take pictures of your automobile from several angles, capturing the damage to both cars, to fully document the collision. It is also a good idea to take images of the license plate of the opposing vehicle. You can provide pictures to your insurer to substantiate your claim during the claims process.


5. Record people involved


Remember to add the names of all passengers in the other car. You must provide the names and addresses of everyone involved. You should also include the names and contact details of any witnesses to the accident, if there were any.



6. Communicate without assigning blame


Even though you should always tell the other driver what happened, you should be careful not to blame or apologize.


Did you know that just expressing "I'm sorry" could be seen in some circumstances as an admission of legal responsibility


7. Submit a claim to your insurance provider


You should submit an auto insurance claim as soon as you can after the accident.


This will enable your claim to be processed more quickly. Also, if you call your auto insurance company early, you will be better protected if the other driver makes false claims about injuries or damage. You can submit a claim with the Tennessee Auto Insurance Agency via phone or online.


Commonly asked questions


Can I purchase insurance after an accident?


You can purchase insurance and find insurance providers whenever you wish. However, you cannot buy insurance for repairs after an accident.


What to do if the accident was your fault?


Following an accident you believe was your fault, you would take the actions outlined above and file a claim with your insurance provider.


Even if you think you are at fault, the insurance adjuster's inquiry will evaluate your legal liability first. Repairs may be covered regardless of fault if you have comprehensive and collision insurance.


What to do if you were not the cause of the accident?


Even if the accident was not your fault, you must submit a claim to your insurance provider. If the other motorist is determined to be at fault, the other driver's insurance company may be obligated to pay for repairs, depending on your state's laws. Yet, some states do not recognize blame, in which case both insurers would be responsible. Consult your insurance provider if you need clarification on whether your state is no-fault.


And keep in mind that legal liability is only established after an investigation, even if you believe you are not at fault.


How does an insurance company assess car damage?


Insurance companies estimate the cost of repairing your car. However, depending on your insurance coverage, you can get that money back after paying a deductible.


Your car might be deemed unrepairable if the repair costs are too high. In this situation, depending on the coverage of your particular policy, you can be compensated for the current market value of your car.


What occurs after I submit a claim to my insurance provider?


Your insurance carrier will require the data listed earlier when you submit a vehicle insurance claim. Also, they will designate an adjuster to examine your car for damage to assess who was responsible for the collision and the cost of repairs.


Depending on your insurance, you might be compensated for the repairs or, if your car is totaled, for its real cash value.


In conclusion


Accidents happen, and they are frightening. Kudos for learning to be ready for an accident by taking these seven actions. Reviewing your insurance policy to ensure you have the proper auto insurance and coverage for what you require is one thing you can do right away to help in the event of an accident.

html:
What To Do If Your Car Is Stolen

You must act fast as soon as you realize your car has been stolen. This article will guide you on what to do if your car is stolen so that you can recover it as quickly as possible.


Although there are no guaranteed ways to ensure the safe return of your stolen car, following this advice will keep you calm and hasten the investigation and insurance claim procedure.


1. Make a police call right away


Call the police when you confirm that your vehicle was stolen, not just towed, or that you forgot where you parked.


Fortunately, the police find 35% of stolen cars on the same day and 45% within two days.


The police will ask you the following questions:


  • Your car's make, model, year, and color

  • Any distinctive qualities of your vehicle registration number

  • Vehicle's license plate number (VIN)

  • Let them know if you have a GPS-tracking system

  • Where you last saw your vehicle

  • When you last saw your vehicle

  • A description of your neighborhood

  • An approximate time you guess the car was stolen.


2. Call your auto insurance provider


Call your auto insurance provider within 24 hours of the theft or when you have filed a police complaint. Next, make a claim with your insurance company. You must get the information to your insurance company as soon as possible. Tennessee Auto Insurance Agency customers can submit a claim online in under ten minutes.


Your insurance provider will ask you the same questions the police asked, and they will also ask the following:


  • A list of any other valuables that were in your car, for example, a laptop or other electronic devices, sports equipment, literature, or tools, along with a brief description of each item

  • A copy of the police report


You must realize that you may not find your car.



Only half of the stolen cars are found. This is because vehicles are often stolen for their parts and can be easily disassembled. If your car is found, it may be damaged. The thieves may have removed some parts.



3. Check your vehicle carefully if it is returned


If your automobile is returned to you and is still drivable, you should thoroughly inspect it first. Put on some rubber gloves, use a flashlight, and go through your car looking for anything that does not belong to you. Inform the police of everything you discover. You do not want anyone to get wounded, and you do not want to get stopped for anything out of the ordinary. For example, there can be contraband or goods used in crimes in the car. So again, inform the police about everything you discover.



4. Future protection for your automobile


The moment has come to consider adopting new steps to dissuade potential thieves from ever again touching your car. For example, consider anti-theft tools like a modern alarm system or a GPS tracking device.


5. Verify the scope of your auto insurance


Comprehensive insurance, which is an optional plan, typically covers auto theft. However, the state's minimum auto insurance requirements usually do not cover car theft.


Remember that your auto insurance does not cover personal items in your vehicle. They must be covered, or you must make a claim on your renters' or homeowners' insurance.


Commonly asked questions


How can I find my stolen vehicle?


There are several ways to find your stolen car:


  • First, inform the police about the license plate

  • Next, review the vehicle's maintenance history report (VIN)

  • Then, with the built-in Bluetooth tracking system, locate the location.

  • Use the GPS tracker that is already inside the car to find it.



What does a car's anti-theft device do?


An anti-theft system works to either deter thieves from stealing your car or assist in finding and recovering it if theft occurs. Simple auditory car alarms to more sophisticated car tracking systems are all examples of devices.



How long, on average, does it take to locate a stolen car?


Usually, a stolen car is discovered by the police 48 hours after it was reported missing. Nonetheless, the procedure could go on for a very long time. Thus, have patience as the police look for your car.


What do criminals do with stolen vehicles?


According to the police, car thefts have three motives: joyrides, profit-driven sales or scrapping, or other criminal activity. The police explained that car thieves are always on the prowl for many reasons, so you must always pay attention to the security of your car.


How can I keep someone from stealing my car?


  • Lock the doors and shut the windows of your car.

  • Keep your automobile keys safe.

  • Place your automobile in a safe location.

  • Keep your car protected; take anything valuable from the vehicle.

  • Set off your vehicle's alarm.

  • Install safety equipment.

  • Make certain that your car is adequately insured with Tennessee Auto insurance agency.


What happens if your vehicle is not found?


If you have comprehensive insurance, your insurer will cover the value of your automobile at the time it was stolen if it is not discovered. Moreover, comprehensive claims have a deductible (the amount that gets subtracted from a claim payout). This means that if your lost automobile was worth $15,000 and you had a $1,000 deductible, you would get a reimbursement of $14,000.


An insurance company will analyze your current service records and receipts for any repair work to determine the value of your car. To obtain the most accurate quotation, be sure to provide your insurance with any supporting documentation you may have.


Depending on the insurance agency's assessment, an automobile can typically be classified as "fair," "excellent," or "outstanding. The agency would respond 'excellent' if you can establish that the vehicle was well maintained and in good shape.


What happens if your car is found?


When a vehicle goes missing, the police are typically the ones who discover it. When you are ready to pick it up, the police will contact you and have it impounded. Inform the police if you find your automobile first.


Whoever finds your automobile, get in touch with your insurance provider right away. Your insurer becomes the vehicle owner if it is recovered after a settled claim. If you still need to purchase a replacement, you may have the opportunity to purchase your automobile back.


Get out to your home or renters insurance provider to let them know you have your belongings back if the found vehicle contains any personal goods that you had previously reported stolen. This enables it to update your claim and inform you of the subsequent actions.


In conclusion


Call the police and your auto insurance agency if your car is stolen. Give them all the information they ask for. When the vehicle is found, have your car inspected to ensure it is safe to drive, just in case any parts are missing or if it is identified while your claim is still being processed. Also, you should use a flashlight to search your car for items that are not yours.


Furthermore, remember that your comprehensive insurance will cover any repairs to your automobile caused by the theft.

title: Factors That Affect Your Car Insurance Rate
metaDescription: Factors that affect your car insurance rates   Many people often ask why their car insurance rates change.
excerpt: Factors that affect your car insurance rates Many people often ask why their car insurance rates change. html:
Factors that affect your car insurance rates


Many people often ask why their car insurance rates change. Although it could appear random, there are valid explanations for why the pricing fluctuates.


Some reasons include: adding extra drivers to your policy, filing claims, your driving record, and your credit score. This article will discuss some factors leading to insurance price fluctuations. We will also give tips on how to reduce insurance costs.


1. Your driving history


Even if you are not at fault, car accidents, speeding tickets, reckless driving, and drunk driving could raise your premiums. Let's compare the amount of driving during and after the pandemic. People started staying at home because of the pandemic in early 2020. In general, they were driving less, which reduced the number of accidents. However, people began reverting to pre-pandemic habits in 2021, such as going out more frequently. Generally speaking, more accidents are likely when more cars are on the road. Moreover, the severity of car accidents has increased.



2. Your car


A new car typically costs more to fix after an accident. Also, new vehicles are more vulnerable to theft or break-ins. Talk to your insurance provider about how your rates will change if you purchase a new car. Remember that some types of vehicles are also highly susceptible to theft. Thieves also prey on cars with expensive parts.


3. Adding a driver to your coverage


All the above factors may affect your rate if you add another driver to your policy. As you might expect, the high risk of new drivers can generally increase your speed, especially if you add a young driver.


4. Data specific to your area


When figuring out your rate, insurance companies look at more than just your car and how you drive. For example, the following things may cause your insurance bill to go up for no apparent reason:


Criminal activity

Risk of natural disasters

Insurance fraud

Risk of accidents

Uninsured or underinsured drivers on the road


5. Inflation


Due to labor shortages and problems in the supply chain, auto repair prices have risen. When calculating premiums, insurance firms must consider these increases.


The value of most automobiles is increasing, whether new or used, which is another factor affecting the auto insurance market. Used automobile costs have increased by 26.4%, while new car prices have increased by about 9.8%.


There are a few reasons for this. First, the demand for cars, SUVs, trucks, and their parts has increased while the supply is decreasing worldwide. And you know, there is always a demand for new cars.


Furthermore, critical parts like semiconductors, which are needed for the processors in modern cars, could not be made during the pandemic, reducing the number of cars on the market.


Although production has begun, there is still a need for more compared to the demand that has been building. As a result, many new automobiles and the parts used to make them are also languishing on ships and docks in the United States, waiting to be trucked to dealerships and manufacturers nationwide.


Consequently, repairs and replacements cost more since cars and parts are more expensive. So the average car insurance claim price has since increased.



6. Changes in discount policies


When you purchase your first policy with a car insurance company, they might give you an introductory discount. Check your statement and contact your insurance provider if you have any questions.


Comparing shops to ensure you are receiving the greatest deal is crucial. For example, many different auto insurance savings are available from Tennessee Auto Insurance Agency, ranging from going paperless to getting a new policy before your current one expires. In addition, you can tailor your insurance so that you only pay for what you need and receive discounts. Click here to get a quote.


Your options for lowering insurance prices


There are things you can do to assist in keeping insurance price hikes in check, even though some of them are beyond your control.


Driving safely and responsibly is advised. Ensure that everyone covered by your insurance follows the rules of the road and drives carefully, especially in challenging situations and bad weather. This will help you avoid getting tickets and having accidents that raise your insurance costs.


Enroll in telematics


Why not use telematics to save money if you and the others covered by your policy drive defensively and safely? Telematics continuously gathers data about your driving patterns. If you sign up for a telematics program, you can save money on the first few months of your car insurance. Safe driving practices can result in savings at renewal, while riskier practices could result in a higher premium.


Modify your settings to be a digital customer


Customers who participate digitally may see their premiums reduced. These discounts are given to paperless customers who sign up through the carrier's app.


Study the coverage


Review your auto insurance and other coverage with your insurance agent. They can determine that you are carrying extra or redundant protection. They might also have some suggestions for ways to reduce the cost of your insurance.


Increase the deductible


Increasing your deductible can frequently reduce premiums. But remember that the deductible will be your responsibility out-of-pocket, so you should always keep enough cash on hand to pay it in case you need to file a claim.


Look for specials


Check to see if you are eligible for discounts, such as those for having more than one policy, using EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer), or being a good student.


Make the most of your car insurance


Find out if your insurance company can give you extra perks for driving safely on top of the standard coverage. For example, Tennessee Auto Insurance Agency offers: Multi policy discounts, transfer discounts, and multi vehicle discounts.


In conclusion


Factors that may affect car insurance prices are sometimes out of your control. However, some common reasons for price increases are recently filed claims under your policy, traffic tickets, and driving while intoxicated.


The prices can also increase if there are more claims in your neighborhood. In that case, there may be more weather-related mishaps, higher theft rates, more vandalism, or other problems that the insurer must pay for. Or if you relocated to a location with a higher crime risk than where you were previously a resident.

I have decided to sell my car. What do I do now?


Need help knowing where to begin when trying to sell your car? In this article, you will discover all the information you need to assist you in making your decision. For example, how do you handle car insurance, how much is its value, and how do you get it ready for sale?


You feel it is time for you and your car to part ways. Your vehicle has provided excellent service, and you have become attached to it. Whether you are relieved to let it go or ready to say goodbye, this article will help you decide on the best ways to approach the process. Continue reading for vital information on how to sell your car, prepare your automobile for sale, and how the sale will affect your auto insurance.


What is the best way to sell my car?


You have three options, and the first two—selling it yourself or exchanging it at a dealership—are the most popular. The third option is not as popular but merits consideration—selling your vehicle to car selling website. Each choice has its benefits and drawbacks. Now let's weigh the options.


I think I should sell my car myself


The advantage of selling your car this way is that it will make you the most profit. It is the best option if you are willing to do the work. However, you must know how to advertise, research, and negotiate with people. Because selling your car yourself is time-consuming, it might not be a suitable method if you are busy.


I think I should trade my car in at a car dealership


Trading your car at a dealership saves you the hassle of finding a buyer—no need to post ads or negotiate with strangers. The disadvantage is that the dealer often has the upper hand simply because they know more, so you might pay more for the new car.


I think I should sell my car to a Car-selling website

Once again, if you sell your car to a car-selling website, you avoid all the headaches of dealing independently. Depending on where you stay, you may take your vehicle to them for an appraisal or obtain a fast offer online. In any case, you immediately receive a written, no-obligation offer valid for a few days. The good thing about this is you have these days to compare it with what a dealership offers, and you have a starting point for negotiations if you decide to sell to friends.


What is the value of my car?



Knowing your car's value is essential because it helps you know your asking price. You must decide on an asking price before you sell your car or know how much you can anticipate receiving for your trade-in at the dealership. But how do you find out the value of your vehicle?


You can take your vehicle to a dealer or a website that sells cars, such as CarMax or CarWow, for an appraisal if you prefer face-to-face interactions. Car-selling websites have a systematic approach because they purchase many vehicles annually. Therefore, you can accept their written, personalized offer and get the money instantly or think about it for a few days.


Alternatively, you can use websites that estimate the value of your car. Unfortunately, many websites offer vague estimates, and some try to connect you with dealers.


Some car-selling websites may inform you of the price they are prepared to pay for your vehicle, but this may not reflect its actual market value. You can therefore use the price as a starting point for talks with dealerships and individual purchasers even if you decide not to sell your car on these websites.


What documents do I need to sell my car?


You should always check the state's DMV website to double-check that you have all the essential papers for your car. States have different laws. However, here is a short list of documents you should acquire to assist in selling your automobile more quickly or successfully.


  • Title. The car is yours if you hold the title. Just sign the deal and give it to the buyer to complete it. However, you might need to contact your bank or loan business to complete the transaction if you don't have the title.

  • A valid photo ID for all owners

  • Valid vehicle registration

  • All the keys and fobs of the car


Additionally, provide simple facts about your car. Vehicle identification numbers, sale bills, maintenance records, and certificates will make your transactions easier. Although providing this extra information is not a legal requirement, it gives the buyer assurance about the quality of the car.


Remember that you and the buyer are responsible for certain things during and after the sale. So, once more, visit the DMV website to see the precise requirements for closing the deal.


How can I prep my car for sale?


If you plan to sell the automobile, getting it polished or cleaning it will increase its visual appeal. Furthermore, you want to think about addressing any recognized mechanical issues.



You can remove all personal stuff if you are trading in your automobile or selling it to the car dealer, but cleaning is not required. Most automobile buyers are more focused on long-term maintenance. Therefore, when figuring out your assessment offer, they put a lot of emphasis on the car's long-term upkeep and overall care.


What happens to my car insurance when I sell?


Many people make the mistake of canceling their auto insurance when they decide to sell their cars. Canceling your auto insurance before selling the car is a wrong move. Driving without insurance carries harsh fines and punishments. So as long as the vehicle is in your name, keep at least the bare minimum of coverage. You are responsible for injuries or damages caused by anyone operating a car still in your name.


After you have sold your car and all papers have been signed, cancel or terminate your current auto insurance coverage as soon as possible. This is also true if you traded your old car for a new one.


Get new auto insurance for your new vehicle. The insurance rate might change depending on the nature of your new ride. When you quote with Tennessee Auto Insurance Agency, you can customize your insurance to only pay for what you need. Click here to get a quote


Be careful some private buyers may ask that you extend your auto insurance for a few days or weeks. Do not. All claims will be rejected as soon as you transfer ownership. The buyer needs to get auto insurance. At Tennessee Auto Insurance Agency, we insure you for less.


In conclusion


If you have decided to sell your car, you can try selling it yourself, contacting a dealer, or selling it on a car-selling website. Before selling your car, you must know the value of your car. To estimate your car’s worth, try to estimate how much car-selling websites are willing to pay for your car. Additionally, ensure you have all your documents sorted out so the transaction can go smoothly.

So what does "full coverage" car insurance actually mean?

When financing or leasing a vehicle, your lender may use the term "full coverage." That means they require you to carry comprehensive and collision plus anything else your state mandates. Liability is a mandatory coverage in nearly every state, while comprehensive and collision (physical damage coverages) are optional. However, lenders can have their own rules about the coverages they require. Learn more about car insurance requirements by state and liability vs. full coverage car insurance.

Instead of asking, "Is my car insurance full coverage?" ask your insurance company or agent if you have the right coverages. Paying for every protection offered by your insurance company could get expensive. While your lender may consider the state-minimum liability as sufficient, that may not be enough coverage to protect you and the other drivers on your policy. You might consider customizing coverages for you, your family, and your vehicle. Click GET A NEW AUTO QUOTE

Should I add optional coverages?

Even if your lender doesn't require any coverage, a new vehicle is an important investment and should be protected. Comprehensive and collision will pay for damages to your vehicle due to accidents and incidents in and out of your control. If your vehicle's value is minimal (less than $2,000), carrying physical damage coverage may not make sense. Should you decide to select liability coverage only, make sure you'll be able to purchase a new vehicle out of your pocket in the event it's totaled and uninsured.

Extra coverage like roadside assistance or rental car reimbursement is typically inexpensive and can be purchased at your discretion as well.

How much is full coverage insurance?

Adding physical damage protection and other optional coverages will cost more than a liability-only policy. How much more depends on many factors, including the year, make, and model of the vehicle you want to protect, plus the car insurance deductible you select — the cost of comprehensive and collision coverage will decrease if you choose a higher deductible.

title: what insurance steps to take after car Accident?
metaDescription: car insurance accidents
excerpt: What to Do After a Car Accident in Tennessee Call 911 and wait for the police to arrive. Exchange contact information and start gathering evidence. Get medical attention as soon as possible. Notify your insurance company, but be cautious.
html:
What to Do After a Car Accident in Tennessee

  1. Call 911 and wait for the police to arrive.

  2. Exchange contact information and start gathering evidence.

  3. Get medical attention as soon as possible.

  4. Notify your insurance company, but be cautious..

  5. Contact a Tennessee car accident lawyer.



Call the State of TN Auto Accident Call Center immediately at (855) 253-0629 with date, time, and location of the incident, as well as any additional information you may have. Take photos of both vehicles, as well as the license plate and VIN tag of the other vehicle (on the driver-side dash, near the windshield).

Do you have to call the police after an accident in Tennessee?

In Tennessee, you are not required to report car accidents that do not result in injuries or cause only very minor property damage. However, you are required to report accidents that result in death, personal injury or property damage exceeding $400.


Is Tennessee a no fault state for accidents?

Tennessee is considered a “fault state,” meaning that if you are injured in a car accident here and another driver is at fault, you may be able to recover damages from them and from their insurance company in a personal injury suit. https://www.insuringyouforless.com/automobile

Is there a time limit to report a car accident to the police?

You need to report an accident to the police by dialing 101 – the police non-emergency number – within 24 hours. If you cause any damage to someone's vehicle or property, no matter how minor, you should stop.

How long does an accident stay on your record in Tennessee?

Tennessee is a fault state, so you might wonder if that can affect the length of time car accidents remain on your driving record. Although there are several factors that can determine the penalties you can face if you were responsible for an accident, the accident will stay on your record for three years.

How many points is an at fault accident in TN?

Improper turning: 3 points. Failure to yield the right-of-way: 4 points. Leaving or fleeing the scene of an accident: 5 points, called “car accident” points. Reckless driving can net you 6 “reckless driving” points.

html:
What does liability insurance in Tennessee Cover?

Liability insurance pays to repair or replace the other driver's car, or other damaged property, and pays other people's medical expenses when you're at fault in an accident. If you still owe money on your car, your lender will require you to have collision and comprehensive coverage.

GET A FREE QUOTE TODAY

What is all included in liability insurance?

Liability coverage includes property damage and bodily injury coverages. Property damage covers damage to the other party's property. This could include damage to vehicles, a yard, light pole, or other property damaged because of the accident.


What is proof of Tennessee liability insurance?

A standard proof of liability insurance form promulgated by the Tennessee Department of Insurance and issued by a liability insurer that includes: (A) The name of the insurer; (B) The insurance policy number; (C) The policy period (dates of coverage and issued for 30 days or more); (D) The name and address of each insured .


What are the minimum liability coverage requirements in Tennessee?

According to state law, Tennessee drivers need to have minimum insurance coverage of $25,000 per injured person, up to at least $50,000 per accident. Additionally, Tennessee drivers must have coverage for property damage of at least $15,000.

What happens if someone else is driving my car and gets into an accident in Tennessee?

In Tennessee, the car insurance of the party at fault for causing the collision is financially responsible for damages. If your friend was at fault for causing the crash, therefore, your auto insurance company will pay for victims' medical bills and property repairs.

What is typically not covered under liability insurance?

Liability insurance provides protection against claims resulting from injuries and damage to people and/or property. Liability insurance covers legal costs and payouts for which the insured party would be found liable. Provisions not covered include Intentional damage, contractual liabilities, and criminal prosecution.

You don’t want to face a problem in your apartment or rental home. But, sometimes you can’t avoid it. And if something happens that damages your property, you could have to get out of the house for a while. Luckily, if you have appropriate renters insurance, you might have assistance available.

Renters insurance often provides expenses protection. Still, coverage can get a bit complicated. Make sure you understand the ins and outs by examining your policy closely.

Renters Expenses Insurance

If a damaging accident occurs in your home, it might make it unsafe to live in or use fully. Therefore, you might have to go to a hotel, eat out for a while, or take a few excursions you didn’t plan on. In situations like these, expenses insurance might be able to help you out.

Say, for example, that your apartment burns because of an electrical fire. It was not your fault, but the apartment sustains a considerable amount of damage. Your renters possessions insurance might pay to help you replace belongings lost in the fire. The property owner’s structure coverage will then pay to repair the property. But the repairs will take time. You won’t be able to live in the apartment because it is structurally unsafe.

This is where renters insurance expenses protection might come in handy. Most renters policies contain this coverage. So, when you move out of the apartment for the repair period, this coverage can help you out. It might pay some or all of your expenses until you can move back into the property.

Limits Exist

Renters expense coverage is important to have in place. Nevertheless, it usually won’t cover 100 percent of the costs of your expenses following accidents.

· Your policy often won’t pay when accidents were not the result of a peril or hazard covered by your policy. For example, if you have to move out because your HVAC system failed in the middle of a heat wave, you likely won’t have coverage.

· Most policies will set maximum amounts of money that they will pay for your expenses. So, you’ll likely still have to shoulder a few of your costs on your own.

· Many policies only provide living expenses protection for a defined period. For example, this might be 30 days. Therefore, if you have to stay out of the home longer than this time period, then you’ll still have to pay your own costs.

Ask your Tennessee Auto Insurance agent if you have living expenses coverage attached to your policy. If you have concerns about your ability to afford living expenses if the worst happens, our agents can help you determine the right course of action.

title: Winterize Your Home to Help Prevent Frozen Pipes
metaDescription: Tennessee is home to great music, the Smoky Mountains, Nashville hot chicken and generally mild weather—except during the winter. Beginning around December, temperatures often drop, causing many homeowners to have frozen water pipes.
excerpt: Tennessee is home to great music, the Smoky Mountains, Nashville hot chicken and generally mild weather—except during the winter. Beginning around December, temperatures often drop, causing many homeowners to have frozen water pipes.
html:
Tennessee is home to great music, the Smoky Mountains, Nashville hot chicken and generally mild weather—except during the winter. Beginning around December, temperatures often drop, causing many homeowners to have frozen water pipes. Fortunately, homeowners can take preventative action to help prevent frozen water pipes and, hopefully, avoid damage to their homes.

Seven Tips for Winterizing Your Home

Below are seven preventive measures you may take to winterize your home, helping to ensure your water pipes can handle the colder temperatures.

1. If temperatures are below freezing, allowing your faucets supplied by exposed pipes to drip slowly can keep water flowing and help prevent freezing. Make sure to shut off the faucets when the temperatures rise and the threat of freezing ends.

2. If you are leaving for a while, turn off and drain any in-ground sprinkler system that you may have. You should also consider leaving your house’s heat set at no lower than 55 degrees Fahrenheit.

3. Disconnect and put away outdoor hoses.

4. Wrap any outside faucets.

5. If you have water supply lines in your garage, keep your garage doors closed as much as possible.

6. Routinely open the cabinet doors in your kitchen and bathrooms to circulate warmer air around the plumbing.

7. If your house has exposed pipes (to the cold), consider wrapping them with insulation or use a UL-listed electric heat cable in accordance with instructions to help keep the pipes warm.

Even though you may take these precautions, sometimes pipes still freeze and additional steps must be taken. These steps are discussed next, including if you experience pipe damage.

You Have Damage—Now What?

If you have frozen pipes or water damage, you should immediately shut off your water by turning off the main shut-off valve. Consider using warm air to thaw your pipes; you can do so with a space heater or hair dryer, but make sure you use those items following their manufacturer’s recommendations. Additionally, don’t leave electrical heaters unattended or use any open flames.

Contact your insurer immediately if your home has damage from a burst pipe and take photos or record a video of your damage. This evidence may help with your insurance claim. After the insurance adjuster inspects your home’s damage, you may receive a settlement that can be used for repairs.
